This characteristic is 26 apparent in a new study, focusing on people who underwent a hemispherectomy, a surgical procedure in which half of the brain is removed to treat illness. The findings showed that, despite missing half of this critical 27 、participants could function well. This was because the 28 half of their brain strengthened. In fact, researchers found that connections一 and thus communication- between parts of different brain networks are actually stronger in people who had hemispherectomies than in people with intact brains. But a few years after his surgery, scientists found that he could 33 see. They determined that this was because other parts of his brain took over the missing parfs 34 tasks. Another study involved people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes information about smells.
